'Zorvels' is asymmetric..why: A made-up relation (catalogued as zorvels, fictional, no property tags): the word is a nonce verb with no English root and no preposition or morphology that points one way or both, so a model has no default reading of it as asymmetric. A review found that the earlier coinage, 'cobble-sworn to', read as one-way allegiance ('sworn to a lord'); it was replaced for that reason. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, paired with the revision finance-replace-d006 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'; RBox expansion: a made-up relation gets the property the revision changes). The revision changes 'competes with' from symmetric to asymmetric; this insert gives the made-up relation zorvels the revision's new property, asymmetry, so expansion and revision install the same property and differ only in whether an old one (symmetry) had to be pushed out. (literature_arts-insert-d003 gave its made-up relation symmetry, the property at stake, instead; see the report.) The relation and instance pairs are kept from the earlier symmetric version of this record. Asymmetry also allows honest 'no' answers on a fresh relation, which a symmetry insert does not: the first instance asks whether the converse can also hold (no), the second whether the premise rules the converse out (yes). Both are phrased so that a model without the insert gives the opposite answer (a model that knows nothing about the relation would say the converse is possible and is not ruled out), unlike 'Does it follow that ...?', which an unedited model also answers 'no'. Yes and no: direct yes, instances no and yes, cross-lingual (the first instance) no and no (Rule 9, within 1). Before the insert every answer is unknown (original_answer null). The instance pairs join central banks with no special real tie, so only the inserted property gives the answers. Near unrelated asks the same property of a real finance relation whose answer is 'no' (competes_with is symmetric), so an edit that spreads asymmetry to other relations between institutions is caught; far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. The cross-lingual prompts keep the coined verb untranslated. The coined word was changed after review from 'cobble-sworn to' (which reads as one-way allegiance, so answers could come from the word) to the nonce verb 'zorvels', with no English root and no directional morphology; a transitive verb still has a subject and an object, so a slight lean towards 'one-way' cannot be ruled out, and the audit should check the unedited models' answers on the instances before they are relied on (residual risk). The or-side fact was changed from the Bank of Canada's headquarters, whose old evidence had no quote, to a false statement the Wikipedia lead refutes directly. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge.
